resource.name: aws_efs_file_system_policy
resource.description: Provides an Elastic File System (EFS) File System Policy resource.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_efs_file_system_policy` resource enables the management of IAM-based access control policies for Amazon Elastic File System (EFS), allowing users to define permissions and security rules for file system access. Common use cases include enforcing fine-grained access controls, restricting access to specific AWS principals, and ensuring compliance with organizational security requirements. This resource supports configurations for policy statements, role-based access, and conditional rules, making it ideal for securing shared storage in multi-tenant or distributed environments.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an AWS EFS file system policy (`aws_efs_file_system_policy`) to enforce secure transport and define access permissions using an IAM policy document. It showcases the use of the `condition` block to require `aws:SecureTransport` and specifies actions (`elasticfilesystem:ClientMount`, `elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite`) and resources for granular access control.

arguments.name: bypass_policy_lockout_safety_check
arguments.description: (Optional) A flag to indicate whether to bypass the `aws_efs_file_system_policy` lockout safety check. The policy lockout safety check determines whether the policy in the request will prevent the principal making the request will be locked out from making future `PutFileSystemPolicy` requests on the file system. Set `bypass_policy_lockout_safety_check` to `true` only when you intend to prevent the principal that is making the request from making a subsequent `PutFileSystemPolicy` request on the file system. The default value is `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `bypass_policy_lockout_safety_check` argument in the `aws_efs_file_system_policy` resource allows users to override the default safety mechanism that prevents the principal making the request from being locked out of future `PutFileSystemPolicy` operations on the EFS file system. Setting this to `true` enables users to intentionally configure policies that may restrict their own access, typically for scenarios requiring strict access control or delegation, but should be used with caution to avoid accidental lockout.

arguments.name: file_system_id
arguments.description: (Required) The ID of the EFS file system.
arguments.llm_summary: The `file_system_id` argument specifies the unique identifier of the Amazon EFS file system to which the policy will be applied. By defining this required parameter, users associate the resource with a specific EFS file system, enabling the configuration of access control policies that govern permissions and security for the file system.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_efs_file_system_policy` resource represents the unique identifier of the EFS file system policy resource, typically auto-generated by Terraform. While not required, it can be used to reference the policy instance in other parts of the configuration or for tracking and management purposes within the Terraform state.

arguments.name: policy
arguments.description: (Required) The JSON formatted file system policy for the EFS file system. see Docs for more info. The following arguments are optional:
arguments.llm_summary: The `policy` argument in the `aws_efs_file_system_policy` resource allows users to define the JSON-formatted file system policy that governs access control and permissions for the associated Amazon EFS file system. By specifying this argument, users can enforce fine-grained authorization rules, such as IAM-based access policies, ensuring secure and compliant access to the file system in alignment with organizational requirements.
